passage:
It is six o'clock in the morning. William gets up, puts on his sporting suit, and starts jogging right away. He runs to the park and takes morning exercise there. An hour later, he gets on the bus to work.
He is usually busy at work. It takes most of his time to operate the machine of the factory. Although he wants to call up his girl friend, Jane, the job stops him from doing so. When he arrives at the factory, he turns on the switchboard of the power to start the machine. He can't turn it off until four o'clock in the afternoon.
Getting off the bus, William goes back home, takes off the working suit, and sits comfortably on the sofa, picking up the paper from the desk. He enjoys the happy hours.

I got up in the early morning as usual and turned on the radio to listen to English Classroom on the air. I turned it off when the program came to an end. Putting on my uniform and picking up my books from the desk, I went out to wait for the bus. At first I was patient enough to look at each bus passing, trying to find out the number of the bus I was to get on. Little by little I grew impatient, for it was about time for school to begin. It seemed I had to call up my teacher at school and ask for leave.
Right then the bus came, and I at last arrived at school. Everything turned out all right, but I felt tired out.

Annie wanted a puppy, for she liked dogs very much. Annie's classmate, Tina, had five puppies, which had been born the day before. Annie wanted to pick out a puppy for herself, but she had to talk it over with her mother first.
“I have no idea about getting along with a dog. If you can take care of it by yourself, you can keep one,” said her mother.
“Let me think about it,” Annie said. “A dog may be too much trouble, and I will be busy all day long.”
“Take your time,” Annie's mother said. “There is no hurry. The puppy is still quite young.”
That night, when Annie lay down on the bed, she took out a book on “How to Take Care of Your Dog” and read it carefully.
The next day she decided to go to Tina's home and ask Tina for advice. Tina said to her, “It does make some difference to have a dog in a family. A dog will bring a lot of trouble, but sometimes it will bring a lot of fun on purpose, too. That's because most dogs are smart. Since you are busy, it is not wise of you to keep a dog.”

Henry's wedding is to take place next week. Nancy and I have been invited to take part. Yesterday we went downtown together to buy a present for Mary. As it was a holiday, the department store was full of people. Before long, a woman clerk came up to greet us and waited on us.
We intended to buy a dress for Mary, but we thought that Mary had a way of dressing herself. We decided on either an imported watch or a gold bracelet. Both seemed equally good, however. After thinking over which to buy, it made no difference to us. So the clerk put away the imported watch, and we bought the bracelet.
We took a walk after we had bought it. We entered a café at the corner and sat down for a while. We stayed there at least two hours. Although we went back home early, Nancy and I felt rather tired, so we both lay down and took a rest.

There was a medical doctor living in the northern part of the earth. He thought of the warm weather in Miami Beach and made up his mind to spend a vacation for the time being when it was freezing cold in his native land.
He called off all the appointments, prepared for the trip in a hurry and flew to Miami Beach.
The landlord heartily greeted him and shook hands with him. He said, “Is it your first time to be here?” “No, I was here two years ago, and I told myself I would get back some day,” answered the doctor.
“Fine. We have the most beautiful sunshine and weather. People here all enjoy swimming or dancing all day long. By the way, what are you?” asked the landlord. “I'm a doctor. I wonder if people need a doctor here. If so, I would like to stay here for good.” “People here seldom catch cold. Even if they do, they get over it very soon,” said the landlord. “Have a good time, but look out for the pickpockets!”

When we knew that we would have a day off today, Mary and I decided to go on a picnic. This morning, while I was looking over my car, all of a sudden the telephone rang. It was Mary's mother who called. She told me that Mary had a high fever and wanted to call off the appointment with me. As soon as I hung up the receiver, I went off to the garage in a hurry. As I was about to drive to Mary's, I heard Mother calling to me: “John, our answering machine is out of order. Do you mind taking it back to the telephone company?”
“No problem. But I have to hurry up!” I answered.
“Look out for the cars on the way!” Mother continued. I didn't know why she was always thinking of me as a careless boy. When I got to Mary's, her family doctor was about to leave. The doctor told me that Mary had had a fever and coughed at times, and so was obliged to keep on taking medicine. For the time being she was very weak; however, she could count on his prescription to get over her cold.

Far East Department Store has an annual sale now. Mrs. Wang wants to buy a new TV set, but Mr. Wang tries to dissuade her from doing that.
Mrs. Wang: You are always putting me off with words. I'm getting tired of it. When in time shall we have a talk to solve the problem?
Mr. Wang: OK, I decide to buy it this time, but we'd better talk it over because our daily expenditure is quite big. Do you figure it out?
Mrs. Wang: All right. Let me point out a suggestion that we can buy it on time, can't we?
Mr. Wang: Oh, no. I'd rather buy it in cash. In this way, we can save some tax and interest from cash. Isn't it a good idea?
Mrs. Wang: Of course, I can't agree more. Since the sale will be over tomorrow, what do you say to buying it tonight?

Tom and Mary studied in the same college. On a summer afternoon, when Tom went out of the library, he turned around and said to Mary, “You lost your purse. Here it is.” “Oh, thank you. Since the purse is worn out, I'm going to throw it away. Where can I find a garbage can?” said Mary. “Just walk straight and you'll see it on the left.” “Thanks again!” said Mary.
From then on, they paid attention to each other and fell in love very soon. After graduation, they got married. They know that successful marriage has something to do with love and respect. Therefore, they always take turns doing housework and give way to the other's request. As yet, they haven't had any baby, but they really lead a happy life.

Every day our world becomes smaller and smaller. Today jet airplanes fly across the oceans very fast; for example, it is possible to fly from London to New York in three and a half hours on the Concorde jet. We can get in touch with people all over the world via various means of communication. More people travel abroad today. Some businessmen who take charge of quite a few companies have to fly from one country to another. Once in a while you may have a good time visiting the Great Wall of China, taking a trip to the Hawaiian Islands or cruising down the Amazon River. As soon as you wake up, you can watch TV reports about what is going on thousands of miles away. What used to be impossible is now turned into reality. You can no longer make believe that you are living an isolated life. You have to get used to the changes of the modern world and admit that you are one of the villagers of our global village.

Tina is a happy housewife. Besides taking care of her two children, she has to keep house. Her husband is a manager, who is in charge of a computer company, and makes out very well on his job. It's her habit to get up early and clean the rooms. She always does her best to clean until she makes sure that they all look really free from dirt.
Sometimes she will make good time driving to the big city nearby with her husband, and they usually have a good time there. But she likes better to entertain guests at home every now and then. Tina has friends of various kinds, but she has known by heart what their names are and where they come from; therefore, there is no mixing them up. She also gets in touch with her relatives constantly and sees about what they need.
Tina has got so used to being a housewife that she has on no account considered getting rid of the job.

There was a sign outside the door which said: “Keep out of the house!” Last month all at once the house caught fire and was destroyed. No one knows how it happened. It was up to the police chief to decide whether they should look into the case. It seemed out of the question to find out the cause of the fire. But he decided to investigate it. Later, the police noticed that the master in the house kept finding fault with the servant. He called down the servant off and on, for the servant seldom got through with her work.
One time he even took hold of the servant's arm and warned him not to be lazy again. Then the police kept track of what the servant had done. At last the police knew it was the servant who had set the house on fire.

If we keep informed of current events, we'll know wars broke out off and on in the Middle East. It seems to be impossible that there will be peace between Iran and Iraq. More often than not, a whole city will be blown up all at once. All the buildings, whether they are up to date or out of date, are burned down in no time. Though people all over the world feel sorry for the victims, yet they seem to have taken the disaster for granted.
The United Nations has looked into the causes of these wars and scolded publicly those who stirred them up. However, it is not up to this international organization whether both sides should cease fire. As to the reason for the wars, it stands to reason that it is racism. We hope that Iran and Iraq will become reconciled and make good in the reestablishment of friendship.

Although it looked like rain last Sunday, it turned out to be a fine day. Diana and I planned to go shopping. She called for me at one o'clock in the afternoon. She had a nice-looking mini-skirt on. I took a look at her and made believe to faint. Then I pretended to come to. I told her that she should take her age into account and that the mini-skirt was not suitable for her. However, she turned a deaf ear to my words. I gave up persuading her to accept my viewpoint. On the way to the city, our car broke down. A car stopped in front of us, and the driver asked what had become of us. Diana made our problem clear to him. He took pity on us and took us to the nearest garage.

After weeks' planning, our wish to go mountain-climbing and eat out came true at last.
That day when we set out, it looked like rain, but to our relief, it turned out fine. However, having run two or three miles, our car began to make sounds as if it were coughing badly. It was not long before it came to a stop. We all got off, and Father, taking a look at the engine, announced that our car had broken down.
We pushed the car to the side of the highway for Father to fix the engine, but all his efforts were made in vain. We tried to stop each passing car and asked for help, but none seemed to take pity on us. There was nothing for it but to leave our car where it was. We went back home on foot.
We were obliged to give up that day's plan, all because we had not looked after our car well enough. How I felt like crying, and as a matter of fact, that was what my kid sister did. We could only look forward to another trip. I told myself once and for all that nothing like that should take place again.

The sky became gradually overcast, and it seemed likely to rain. No matter how heavily it rained, Mary insisted on going to the party.
She walked on the street under her umbrella. The storm blew so violently that it caused her umbrella to turn inside out.
A gentleman came to her aid. He happened to be one of her boyfriends, Martin, who was taking up medicine at college. With his golden hair and blue eyes, he took after her brother very much. Thinking for a while, she got into his car in the long run.
They had a ride along the smooth highway rather than attending the party. Then they ran out of gas. Martin couldn't but stop at the fuel station.
They went on driving. She took advantage of the chance to talk about her business because she had been out of work for a long time. Perhaps Martin could give her advice. Though Mary didn't go to the party, she had a wonderful day.

I am a student of the Department of Sociology. As I take up old-age problems, I naturally call at the Old People's Home every now and then. Mr. Smith, one of its members, had his wife run over and killed by a truck last year. His son found it hard to get along with him, going off without saying goodbye. Therefore, he was sent to the old people's home and has lived there ever since. Maybe I look like his son; every time I go to see him, he will hold my hands and won't let go. He will ask me to keep in mind that I should take pride in my work and that I should go to see him every month, rain or shine. He likes to talk with me, but our conversation is always cut off by his “Pardons,” for he is hard of hearing. I think that all I can do is ask the supervisor to keep an eye on him.

A: What's wrong with you? You look awful.
B: It's not my day today. In the morning my wife had a quarrel with me because I forgot to shut off the faucet again. Having no time to argue with her, I told her to shut up and hurried to the office. A tire blew out on the way, so I was late when I finally got to the office.
A: Your boss must be mad at you.
B: He warns me that if I do not keep up with other colleagues, I will be fired. He also turns down my new sales project.
A: Don't worry too much. Your boss knows that it is easy to find a new worker, but it is hard to break him in. You have got to be aggressive and on the alert for any fresh ideas about sales. Above all, don't be late again.

As a salesman, I cannot do without a car. I made up my mind to buy one the other day. Before my purchase, I was allowed an hour to try out a car. I was bound for the park and watched out for other cars all the time. Every time I found my car going too near another, I slowed down. All of a sudden, one of the tires blew out on the way. I thought I was bound to get seriously wounded, but luckily it was only my clothes that were torn. A policeman came up to me. He took me for a drunkard and fined me a large sum of money. I used to be shy, but I have grown out of it. So I argued with the policeman. He ignored me and left. Being so unlucky, I guessed I had to make the best of everything.

Five years have passed since I took leave of my hometown. Five years is a long period, but, all the same, I still can't forget my first love. Day in and day out, I have the same dream—I will marry Diana. Being poor in the past, I tried in vain to marry her. Since I have already made a fortune, I don't have to put up with her parents' contempt any longer. There is nothing in the way to stop me proposing to her now. In order to show off my wealth, I will take many jewels with me to go around. Besides, I will put up a stately mansion to live in. I am sure that her parents will be in favor of my proposal now. With all these efforts, I will finally make my dream come true.

When William was three years of age, his father passed away. Because his mother ran away, he was brought up by his pampering grandmother. He grew up to be a teenager too spoiled to tell right from wrong. Except for running errands for his grandmother, he could not be made to take charge of anything, for he was so irresponsible. He just fooled around all day long, doing nothing meaningful. One day he found that he had run out of money. Unable to put up with the inconvenience caused by the lack of money, he held up a taxi, then set fire to it. The taxi driver, knowing him by sight, reported to the police and had him arrested. This is a case of a teenager who got lost. Let it be a warning to every one of us.

My uncle Jim is a successful businessman. He is so well-off that everyone in the town envies him. Unfortunately, he was robbed of most art treasures displayed at home last month. In addition to reporting the robbery to the police, he also hires a detective to help look for those missing treasures. He asks the detective to hand in daily reports so that he may know how things go on. Somehow or other he will find the robber and have him arrested without fail. What he does won't take us by surprise. He is a man of action and determination. Although I am named after him, I will in no way compare with him.

Jack dropped me a line yesterday to the effect that he would quit the job because he could no longer stand for its monotony. As soon as I received his note, I gave him a ring. He said that he stood a good chance of getting a better job. He promised to take pains with his work once he was offered a new one. He would try hard to be a man whom everyone looked up to. I told him that no one would look down upon him as long as he did his best in his work.

Maria: You should have shown up at the party last night. I tried to call you, but no one answered the phone. You must have stayed out late.
Nancy: Well, my uncle went to sea for the first time, so my family all went to see him off.
Maria: It's a pity that you didn't come. I came across our old friend Cindy.
Nancy: Really! I haven't seen her since she moved to another town. How is she going?
Maria: She is fine, and she is still as naughty as a little girl though she has already taken over her father's business. She made faces at me when she first saw me at the party. She still drank to her heart's content.
Nancy: She doesn't change a lot, does she?
Maria: Oh, she is thinner and prettier now. She said that she lost at least ten pounds, so she had to make over all her old clothes.
Nancy: I'm sure now she must have a boyfriend.
Maria: I forgot to tell you that she has married and will give birth to a baby at the end of the year.

I ran across an old friend in the park last week. Twenty years ago he dropped out of our party and set out for the United States to take over a Chinese restaurant. He worked very hard there, getting up early and staying up late. It seemed that the only thing he went in for was making money, and his business made out very well.
Overwork little by little undermined his health. One day he failed to show up in the restaurant as usual and was found lying unconscious in his apartment. He was hospitalized right off and soon brought to. However, he was obliged to keep to his bed for a month. It was during this time that he came to believe in taking a rest after hard work. It didn't make any sense working without having time off, so he made a plan to return to his hometown on vacation, which he carried out with ease.
When departing, he asked me to drop in on him one of these days.

We supposed that if we kept up this speed, we would arrive at Mt. Ali at sunset. Unfortunately, our car suddenly broke down in the middle of the road, so the taxi behind us bumped into our car. Frightened by the bump, my little sister burst out crying. At that time the taxi driver stuck out his head, shouting at us. Instead of trying to get away, we explained to him what had happened. We also let on to him that we were willing to make up for his loss. But he didn't want to meet us halfway. Finally, we paid him a large sum of money to avoid further argument.
I thought it served us right, because we didn't check up the car in advance. Well goes the saying that it is easy to be wise after the event.

Last week my brother was knocked out by a falling rock when camping and got badly hurt. So he didn't go to school the whole week. He is obliged to make up all the lessons he missed. He has been getting all A's and standing out from all the others in his class. Nevertheless, he is afraid he may not be able to keep up with his classmates this time because of his long absence. He was so discouraged that I tried to cheer him up. I told him that if he stuck to every lesson with all his heart, he would surely make out very well. He promised me to work harder. I believe he won't stick me and will do his best to live up to his promise now that nothing goes wrong with him. Of course, he still needs some tonic to build up his strength lest something unexpected should come about.

Sales had been falling off recently. Workers had to be laid off, and plans to modernize the equipment fell through. The president of the company was advised to turn over the business to his son. To everyone's disappointment, the advice was ruled out because he had it in for his son. To save the company from becoming bankrupt, his family tried to talk him into giving up the post and finally had it out with him. The president felt he couldn't hold out any longer and gave in to the pressure.

A. Another hour had passed and it still went on raining without letting up. Mr. Wang borrowed from the host an umbrella, which he said he would bring back next time. When he arrived home, it was already midnight and his wife was still waiting up for him. Without saying anything, his wife handed him a note, which he read over. His wife warned him that if he came home so late again, she would break off their marriage. He thought he had better let her alone for a while. He would wait until she was not angry and then explain to her.
B. On the whole, the heels of the shoes brought out by their company wear down easily. As a result, the new product does not sell well. The company has no choice but to lay off the workers, let alone raise their wages.

For a long time Paul had had his heart set on taking a trip around the world. To get enough money for the trip, he worked out some plan to sell out all his properties by the sea, including a summer cottage looking out on the Pacific Ocean. As he had never done such a thing before, he was afraid that he might be cheated; therefore, he turned to a cousin of his, who was cut out to be an estate agent.
This cousin of his was indeed a cute fellow. Every time a prospective buyer came to him, he was all set to try to talk the buyer into buying some of the properties. Instead of coming straight to the point, he would often begin by beating about the bush and tactfully stir up the buyer's desire in the end. Soon all Paul's properties were sold for a considerable sum of money, with which he happily set forth on his trip.

Mark: My father used to tell me to beware of bad company. But I did not catch on to what he said at that time. I just fooled around, doing nothing meaningful.
Joe: Ten to one, you must have kept bad company since you ignored your father's advice.
Mark: You are right. I was taken in by my friend. I have lost a large sum of money, and now my property is at stake.
Joe: What a pity! I know how you feel. Would you tell me what you are up to?
Mark: I want to put an end to my present difficult situation. So, to tell you the truth, I would like to get even with him. I will go on carrying out my plan of revenge even though I may stir up trouble.
Joe: You are beside yourself with anger now. Cool down! Remember to look before you leap.
